facts.raw_span: multiple painless nodules on the fingers of both hands
vesicles that ruptured and formed hemorrhagic crusts
discomfort and pain along the medial aspect of his right arm and forearm
denied trauma or insect bites
his cow had similar lesions on its teats
3–4 firm, non-tender nodules with central hemorrhagic crusts and surrounding erythema
mild tenderness and increased warmth along the medial right arm and forearm
Dermoscopy (10×) of one nodule showed an erythematous area with central ulceration and crust
yellow-white streaks, brown dots, a structureless whitish area partially surrounding the ulcer, an erythematous ring, and dot vessels

concepts.why: The patient's presentation of painless nodules on the fingers, vesicles that ruptured and formed hemorrhagic crusts, and the presence of similar lesions on his cow's teats, along with dermoscopic findings, are consistent with Orf virus infection.
The patient's occupation as a dairy farm worker and the presence of similar lesions on his cow's teats, along with the clinical presentation, are consistent with Paravaccinia virus infection.
The patient's exposure to cows with similar lesions and the clinical presentation, including the dermoscopic findings, are consistent with Cowpox virus infection.

The patient's occupation as a dairy farm worker and the presence of a skin lesion with surrounding erythema and increased warmth, along with the clinical presentation, are consistent with Erysipeloid.
The patient's presentation of skin lesions on the fingers, along with the absence of trauma or insect bites, could be consistent with Contact dermatitis.
The patient's presentation of firm, non-tender nodules with central hemorrhagic crusts and surrounding erythema could be consistent with Psoriasis.
The patient's presentation of skin lesions on the fingers, along with the clinical presentation, could be consistent with Dermatophytosis.
The patient's presentation of discomfort and pain along the medial aspect of his right arm and forearm, along with the clinical presentation, could be consistent with Vasculitis.
